title: SB 271 (2021 Regular Session): AN ACT relating to voting.
operative_text:
(a_in_person_id)
(section) Sec. 3 (KRS 117.085(1)(e))
(quote) if the voter provides proof of identification as defined in KRS 117.375 or meets the requirements of KRS 117.228 and 117.229[, and the voter:
(section) Sec. 9 (KRS 117.228(1))
(quote) on the day of a primary, an election, or during in-person early[absentee] voting, if a voter is unable to provide proof of identification as required under KRS 117.225, and as defined under KRS 117.375, a voter may cast a ballot if the individual:
(b_no_id_remedy)
(section) Sec. 9 (KRS 117.228(1)(c)8.)
(quote) The voter has one (1) of the following impediments to procure proof of identification as defined in KRS 117.375: a. Lack of transportation; b. Inability to obtain his or her birth certificate or other documents needed to show proof of identification; c. Work schedule; d. Lost or stolen identification; e. Disability or illness; f. Family responsibilities; g. The proof of identification has been applied for, but not yet received; or h. The voter has a religious objection to being photographed.
(section) Sec. 9 (KRS 117.228(2))
(quote) In addition to the requirements of subsection (1) of this section, to cast a ballot, the voter who is unable to provide proof of identification shall provide to an election officer: (a) The voter's Social Security Card; (b) Any identification card issued by a county in this state ... (c) Any identification card with the voter's photograph and the name of the voter stated; (d) Any food stamp identification card, electronic benefit transfer card, or supplemental nutrition assistance card ...; or (e) A credit or debit card with the name of the voter stated.
(section) Sec. 10 (KRS 117.229)
(quote) the voter may cast a provisional ballot for the federal elective office of President, Vice President, United States Senator, and United States House of Representative if the individual conforms to the provisional voting requirements in accordance with the Help America Vote Act of 2002.
(c_mail_ballot_id)
(section) Sec. 3 (KRS 117.085(1)(a)2.a.-c.)
(quote) a. The secure online portal shall have the capacity to ensure verification of the identity of the voter through an identity document, as defined in KRS 186.010, on file with the Kentucky Transportation Cabinet; b. If a voter does not have an identity document on file with the Kentucky Transportation Cabinet, and does not have proof of identification as defined under KRS 117.375, the voter may confirm his or her identity as required under KRS 117.227 by completing the voter's affirmation under Section 9 of this Act, and provided on the secure online portal; and
(section) Sec. 3 (KRS 117.085(1)(a)2.c.)
(quote) c. If the voter does not have an identity document on file with the Kentucky Transportation Cabinet, but has proof of identification as defined under KRS 117.375, the voter shall request an application for a mail-in absentee ballot under paragraph (a)1. of this subsection.
(section) Sec. 3 (KRS 117.085(2)(c))
(quote) Returned to the county clerk either by mail or in-person with[and the voter shall provide] a copy of the voter's[his or her] proof of identification, as defined in KRS 117.375, or the executed voter affirmation as described in KRS 117.228(1)(c), unless the application was completed and returned through the online portal under subsection (1)(a)2. of this section
(section) Sec. 3 (KRS 117.085(6)(e)1.)
(quote) a. The photographed copy of the voter's proof of identification;[ or] b. The number of the identity document on file with the Kentucky Transportation Cabinet; or c. The voter affirmation as prescribed by KRS 117.228(1)(c);
(d_proof_of_citizenship) not stated.
(e_other_rule)
(section) Sec. 9 (KRS 117.228(1)(c)1.)
(quote) The voter is a citizen of the United States;
(other) Sec. 1 (new, ch. 117): cure process for rejected mail-in ballots (missing signature, mismatched signatures, missing witness or assistance form); clerk notifies voter within 3 days; cure due by 4 p.m. on the Thursday after the election.
(other) Sec. 2: KRS 117.066 - allows combining precincts into centralized voting locations.
(other) Sec. 3: KRS 117.085 - online portal for mail-in requests; 'personal preference' added as a reason to vote by mail-in ballot; in-person early voting including two Saturdays; clerks keep ID copy, ID-document number or affirmation for 22 months.
(other) Sec. 4: KRS 117.086 - secure drop box allowed for returning mail-in ballots; drop-box rules.
(other) Sec. 5: KRS 117.087 - more time to process and count mail-in ballots.
(other) Secs. 6-8, 11-12, 14: KRS 117.088, 117.145, 117.165, 117.235, 117.265, 14.312 - conforming and procedural changes (the descriptions and a text search found no ID wording changed there).
(other) Sec. 13: KRS 118.035 - polls open to 8 p.m. prevailing time.
(other) version: orig_bill (the only version): introduced text; slots a-c and the citizen affirmation in e as quoted. No other versions saved.
(other) note: Introduced only; to Committee on Committees; no further action. Bracketed words are deleted. KRS 117.228 and 117.229 are reprinted with one visible change: 'in-person early[absentee] voting' (the list of impediments, the secondary-ID list and the citizen affirmation are unbracketed, so I read them as existing law). New in this bill is the portal ID route in 117.085(1)(a)2. (Transportation Cabinet check; affirmation if no Cabinet ID and no proof of identification; people with proof of ID but no Cabinet record must use a paper application) and the exemption from sending an ID copy when the application went through the portal. 'Proof of identification as defined in KRS 117.375' is not defined in this bill. KRS 117.228 is Sec. 9 and KRS 117.229 is Sec. 10; Sec. 8 amends KRS 117.165.
(note) Off this topic: the bill sets no ID or citizenship-proof rule.
